card.statement:
Once again, Lemma 7.10 can also be deduced from more general considerations related to universal local acyclicity; see [Z4, Theorem A.2.6 and proof of Proposition 5.4.2].

7.6 Construction of the commutativity constraint

Combining Lemma 7.8 and Lemma 7.10, we obtain a canonical isomorphism

$\tau^{\circ}(\mathscr{F}_{1}\star\mathscr{F}_{2})\cong i^{\circ}j_{!*}\,\bigl((\tau^{\circ}\mathscr{F}_{1}\boxtimes\tau^{\circ}\mathscr{F}_{2})|_{U}\bigr),$

(7.8)

valid for any $\mathscr{F}_{1},\mathscr{F}_{2}\in\mathrm{P}_{{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathbf{k})$ . In other words,
the convolution product $\mathscr{F}_{1}\star\mathscr{F}_{2}$ can also be obtained
by a procedure based on the Beĭlinson–Drinfeld Grassmannians $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}$ and $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X^{2}}$ , called the
fusion product.

Let $\mathrm{swap}:\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X^{2}}\to\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X^{2}}$ be the
automorphism that swaps $x_{1}$ and $x_{2}$ .
Then we have $(\mathrm{swap}\circ i)=i$ . Moreover, $\mathrm{swap}$ stabilizes $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X^{2}}|_{U}$ , and under the identification (7.3) the induced automorphism of $(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}\times\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X})|_{U}$ (which we will denote $\mathrm{swap}_{U}$ ) swaps the two factors $\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G,X}$ .
Therefore we obtain canonical isomorphisms

$\displaystyle\tau^{\circ}(\mathscr{F}_{1}\star\mathscr{F}_{2})$
$\displaystyle\cong i^{\circ}j_{!*}\bigl((\tau^{\circ}\mathscr{F}_{1}\boxtimes\tau^{\circ}\mathscr{F}_{2})|_{U}\bigr)$

$\displaystyle\cong i^{\circ}\mathrm{swap}^{*}j_{!*}\bigl((\tau^{\circ}\mathscr{F}_{1}\boxtimes\tau^{\circ}\mathscr{F}_{2})|_{U}\bigr)$

$\displaystyle\cong i^{\circ}j_{!*}(\mathrm{swap}_{U})^{*}\bigl((\tau^{\circ}\mathscr{F}_{1}\boxtimes\tau^{\circ}\mathscr{F}_{2})|_{U}\bigr)$

$\displaystyle\cong i^{\circ}j_{!*}\bigl((\tau^{\circ}\mathscr{F}_{2}\boxtimes\tau^{\circ}\mathscr{F}_{1})|_{U}\bigr)$

$\displaystyle=\tau^{\circ}(\mathscr{F}_{2}\star\mathscr{F}_{1}).$

Restricting to a point of $X$ , we deduce a canonical isomorphism

$\mathscr{F}_{1}\star\mathscr{F}_{2}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathscr{F}_{2}\star\mathscr{F}_{1},$

which provides a commutativity constraint for the category $\mathrm{P}_{{G_{\mathcal{O}}}}(\mathord{\mathrm{Gr}}_{G},\mathbf{k})$ .
card.label: Remark 7.11

paper.title: Notes on the geometric Satake equivalence
paper.abstract: These notes are devoted to a detailed exposition of the proof of the Geometric Satake Equivalence for general coefficients, following Mirkovic-Vilonen.
